Here's a complete English bounty post template you can copy, paste, and adapt. It's designed to be easily parsed by bots (e.g., GitHub Actions, Discord "action board" scrapers) and follows typical Lean/Mathlib collaboration style.

```markdown
[Bounty] $XXX – Formalize (or disprove) the "Prime Emergence Conjecture"

## Problem in plain language
I propose a new conjecture related to prime emergence.  
*(Replace the following with your actual conjecture – keep it concise and precise)*

**Conjecture (natural language):**  
For every integer n > 1, there exists a prime p such that [your precise statement here].

## Formal statement (Lean 4 / Mathlib)
If you already have a Lean formalisation, put it below. Otherwise, a bounty hunter must produce one.

```lean
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime
-- Example placeholder – replace with your own
example (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1) : ∃ p, Prime p ∧ [your predicate] := sorry
```

Bounty goals

Choose one or both:

· A) Formalise the conjecture in Lean + prove it (requires a full proof that compiles with Mathlib).
  Bounty: $___ (paid via GitHub Sponsors / PayPal / crypto)
· B) Disprove the conjecture (provide a counterexample, either in natural language or formalised).
  Bounty: $___

Merge / acceptance criteria

For the bounty to be paid and the contribution merged:

· The work is submitted as a Pull Request to a public GitHub repository (e.g., my own repo or a designated “conjecture-collection” repo).
· The PR includes a clear lean file containing either a proof (with #check) or a concrete counterexample.
· All Lean code passes lean --verify and uses Mathlib 4 (latest stable).
· The PR is merged by me or a designated maintainer.

Optional – to make it "action board" friendly:

· Add label bounty / prime-emergence
· The PR description must contain the exact phrase "Prime Emergence Conjecture bounty"

License

All contributed code will be released under MIT (or CC0 / Apache 2.0). The mathematical statement itself is public domain.

How to claim

1. Fork [my-repo-link] / create a new PR in the target repository.
2. Write your proof/disproof.
3. Reference this bounty post in the PR description.
4. Once merged, I’ll pay the bounty within 7 days.

Contact / discussion

Open an issue in [my-repo-link] or ping me on [Discord/Keybase/Zulip].

```

### 🤖 Tips to make it machine‑scannable for an “action board”

Many bots watch for:

- **Keywords in title**: `[Bounty]`, `$`, `Prime Emergence Conjecture`
- **Checklist syntax**: `- [ ]` (GitHub task list)
- **Label**: add a label like `bounty` or `help-wanted`
- **Exact phrase**: put `"Prime Emergence Conjecture bounty"` in the PR body

If your “action board” is a specific Discord bot or GitHub Project automation, check its documentation – but the template above follows the common pattern used by **GitHub Issues**, **Gitcoin**, and **OnlyDust** bounties.

### ✏️ What you still need to fill in

- Your exact conjecture (replace the placeholder text)
- Bounty amount
- Your GitHub repo link (or specify where the PR should be sent)
- Your payment method

Once you have those, copy the template into a **GitHub Issue**, a **GitHub Gist**, or a **Discord channel** that the bot scans. Good luck!

## Summary (a bounty payout fires for a coupon that has nothing to do with the bounty)

`POST /api/bounties/[id]/claim` only checks that the submitted `coupon_id` **exists**. It never checks that the coupon is actually for the store the bounty is asking about. Any pre-existing coupon id (e.g. `1`, seeded/created for an unrelated store) satisfies the claim, and the route then broadcasts a real `reward_usd` payout from the merchant web wallet.

## Details

In `apps/web/app/api/bounties/[id]/claim/route.ts`:

```ts
const coupons = await db.sql`SELECT * FROM coupons WHERE id = ${coupon_id}`;   // line 30
if (!coupons.length) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Coupon not found' }, { status: 404 });  // line 31

// ...straight to claim + payout, no relevance check:
await db.sql`
  UPDATE bounties
  SET status = 'claimed', coupon_id = ${coupon_id}, claimer_did = ${did}, ...
  WHERE id = ${bountyId} AND status IN ('open', 'funded')
`;                                                                             // line 34-39
// ... prepare-tx + broadcast pays bounty.reward_usd to the claimer          // line 60-83
```

A bounty targets a store via `store_id` **or** free-text `store_name` (`bounties` table, `apps/web/scripts/migrate.mjs:129`), and every coupon has a `store_id NOT NULL` (`apps/web/lib/schema.sql:17`). The claim path compares **neither**. It also never checks that a coupon hasn't already been used to claim a different bounty.

## Impact

- **Payout for irrelevant work.** A bounty created and funded for "a Nike coupon" can be claimed with an existing Amazon coupon (or literally any coupon id). The creator's escrowed `reward_usd` is paid out for a coupon that does not fulfill the bounty.
- **Coupon reuse / wallet drain.** Because there is no "coupon already used" guard, one existing coupon can be used to claim **every** open/funded bounty in sequence, draining the merchant wallet.

This is separate from #35 (which is about `open` vs `funded` status) — it applies even to properly-funded bounties.

## Repro

1. Note any existing coupon id (the migration seeds Amazon/Nike/Walmart coupons; or `POST /api/coupons` one for any store).
2. Find a funded bounty for a *different* store.
3. `POST /api/bounties/{public_id}/claim` with `{ "coupon_id": <that unrelated id> }`.
4. Bounty flips to `claimed`/`paid` and `reward_usd` is broadcast to your wallet.

## Fix (PR opened)

Before marking the bounty claimed: (1) require the coupon's store to match the bounty's `store_id` (or `store_name`), and (2) reject a coupon already used to claim another bounty.
title: Bounty payout fires for a coupon that doesn't match the bounty's store (missing coupon↔bounty validation)

# Background

Polls have two purposes:
1. Quick and easy single selection polls to quickly gather thoughts
2. Ranked choice polls that help to collect detailed feedback. 


We want to be able to support both needs, as detailed below.

# User Stories

## Megan - Group DM Member (simple poll)

Megan is in a group chat with her friends. She wants to be able to quickly ask folks which dress of hers looks best. To do so, she creates a poll. In the poll creation menu, she is able to to upload images and write text next next to them. She is able to set a title and a duration. She also gets to toggle ranked voting and anonymous responses. Finally, she has the option to allow people to select custom responses. 

In this case, she creates a simple poll with no ranked voting and no custom responses. Once Megan hits confirm, a poll appears in the chat. 

### Desktop
On desktop, Megan's friends see a poll appear with each (smaller) image / text option. The header has the title and Megan's profile picture. 

The results are hidden from them until they hit submit. Clicking on each image brings it up bigger with the text as a caption. Users are able to click left or right arrows or use their arrow keys to go between options. Double clicking on the image selects it as the selected choice. They are able to undo that choice by double clicking again. 

Once something is double clicked, a new button on the poll will appear to show results. Results will be shown in order of most to least voted. Next to each option, a pfp of the voters. If the friend clicks on an option again, the same popup is shown, this time with the pfp of the voters in the bottom corner.

After the allotted time, the poll closes. Votes become viewable to all users, and no more votes can be accepted.   

### Mobile
Very similar experience, except in this case, if images are included, clicking on an option pulls up an image carousal that can be swiped through. Holding down on an selects it as an option. 

### Ranked Choice
Ranked choice is similar, except you can select multiple options, It shows you the order selected in both the image carasoul and in the chat. When you view the votes, you get shown the first place selections in order. You can click a button to then see the order changing when 2nd choice votes are added, then 3rd place votes, etc...

## Riley - Moderating Polls (Community)
Riley moderates the Kubuntu community. An anonymous poll was created that contained negative profanity related to the community. They should be able to determine from audit logs what user created what options. If they have a bot that automatically ingests audit logs, that bot should be able to see that as well.

## Andrew - Moderating Polls (Instance)
Andrew is an instance moderator. He received a report of a poll containing negative images. In admin, Andrew is able to view all images associated with the poll. He can take all the same actions as he is normally able to within admin on images. Andrew is also able to delete the poll, see who created it, who created custom answers, and **see who voted on it, even if anonymous**. 

# Thonks
- Anonymous means anonymous votes to the **community**, not anonymous written options or polls.
- Image uploads for polls should follow the same attachment expiries as standard images
- Image uploads need to follow the same API data logging conventions (associated with a messageID, IP, etc..)
- Polls should have their own permission
- There should be a limit to total answers (including custom)
- Would be nice for ranked choice if the bottom most one is dropped when you go to the next layer deep and it has a cute and fun animation

body: **Status: needs mobile and desktop visual design** # Background Threads are one of our top requested features. A common desire on chat platform, akin to breakout rooms for specific sub-conversations, threads are generally considered to be “sub-channels” that sit inside a larger channel. Threads typically have a unique name and a starting message, however the latter should be viewed as optional. We should avoid diverging from industry standard. Nor should we think of threads as a buildup to forums. Both serve different niches. Threads allow for quickly zooming in on a specific message during an active conversation. Forums create hubs for specific types of conversations. While the two products may intersect at a later point, as a MVP to meet user needs rapidly, we should focus our efforts on just implementing a standard “threads feature” # Product needs All designs below (except instance level safety) should be treated as strong suggestions. If you feel you have a better design, we encourage you to explore it, but please understand that if it is not to the team’s liking, we may not accept the end result. Instance level safety designs are requirements. TLDR → Threads are sub-channels. They inherit a large amount of base design and UX from channels. There are specific nuances in the API, database structure, and UX for them, but broadly, they should be treated as channels. ## Initiation - (Desktop) ### Starting a thread * Users should be able to create a thread in any text based channel via three methods: * Hovering over an existing message should display a “thread” icon in the context menu. The thread icon should be in between the reply and the forward icons. A tooltip should appear above with “Start new thread” * If the message is already the start of a thread, this tooltip should instead read “Join thread”, and enter the user into the thread. They should not be able to start a secondary thread. * When right clicking a message or hitting the hamburger icon on a message, a “Start new thread” button should be there. * If the message is already the start of a thread, this tooltip should instead read “Join thread”, and enter the user into the thread. They should not be able to start a secondary thread. * “/thread” in the chat box should allow you to also initiate a thread * When initiating a thread, the creator is presented a popup modal. That modal has: * Thread Name * How long should the thread remain open (default 7d) * Shows a preview of the first message (or nothing if doing /thread) * a confirm and cancel button. * If a user does not have the permissions to start a thread, they will not see any of the buttons or have an autocomplete for /thread * If permissions change while a thread creation modal is open, hitting confirm should fail the user. No special design is needed, but an error message in console is nice. * When a thread is created, the client renders it in the channel as an indented box below the original message * The box should be outlined in the “primary accent” color * The box should have the name of the thread, the last message send timestamp, and the latest message in the thread, and last message author's name & PFP * Coming out of the left of the box should be a line icon similar to the “reply” connecting icon, connecting the thread to the parent message. ### Thread UX * Threads function identically to channels. They should have the same basic design. * A user will not see threads in the channel sidebar until they have joined a thread. However, if an individual clicks on a thread in the chat, they can preview it. Previewing it causes the thread to appear in the channel sidebar (image below), but once a user clicks away from the thread, it disappears. * In the topbar of the thread, the # for the channel name is replaced with the “thread” icon ## Joining a thread - (Desktop) * Threads are joined by being the creator OR by sending a message in the thread OR by hitting one of the buttons defined above * Joining a thread should cause the thread name to appear between the parent channel and the next channel on the list. That should persist while the thread is open. (**see** **Managing Threads - Community Level for information on thread states**) * When a thread is closed or archived, clicking into the thread will put you in the preview state until it is reopened * Closed threads can be re-opened by sending a message or by right clicking the thread in the channel bar and clicking open. * Archived threads cannot be opened except by a moderator * When a thread is un-archived, all members of the thread are automatically rejoined. * Thread names should be indented from parent channel, and should be connected via a line to the parent channel * If a user is in multiple threads, they should appear in order of thread creation * Moderators / admins / those with manage channel perms are **NOT** automatically added to threads. (see **Managing threads - Community Level**) ## Leaving a thread * Once you have joined a thread, you should be able to exit a thread by right clicking the thread in the channel sidebar and selecting a “leave thread” button * This button is only shown when a user is in an open or closed thread. Archived threads do not have this button ## Rollout * After rollout, admins for pre-existing communities should be notified via a pop-up attached to the community name * “Enable threads for your members!” * Clicking the pop-up should clear it. Clicking the community name should also clear it. ## Backend / Quirks * A thread should be treated as a “sub-channel” via the api. Message links within the channel would appear: * `https://fluxer.app/channels/COMMUNITYID/CHANNELID/THREADID/MESSAGEID` * ThreadIDs are a timestamp snowflake of when the thread was started, just like channelIDs * Threads should inherit the same permissions of the parent channel * Threads should inherit the same user notification settings as the parent channel * Anything a user can do in a thread, a bot should be able to do. * Bots should be able to *listen* for thread events. State changes / creations / deletions should send API events. * API Documentation should be updated to reflect this. * Table for messages in the backend should be extended to include an additional column with the ThreadID and ThreadName. * Table for channels should be extended to include an additional column with the ThreadID and ThreadName, as well as the Username and the UserID of the creator at time of creating. * For channels table, parent channel should be included as standard * creation time and creating user should reflect thread not parent channel ## Managing Threads ### Community Level * Community owners / edit community permissions should be allowed to enable / disable threads for specific roles * On rollout, this permission should be automatically turned on for any role with manage community or manage channel permissions in **existing communities** * For new communities post launch, it should be enabled by default for `@everyone` * Individuals with manage channel permissions should be able to do the following: * close thread (can be reopened by anyone sending a message in the thread) * open thread * archive thread (cannot be reopened except by someone with manage channel permissions) * unarchive thread * delete thread * Any individual should be able to see a list of threads in a channel by clicking a thread icon on the top bar of the channel * The thread icon should sit between pinned messages and favorites. * We should remove the notifications setting button * When you click the thread icon, a scrollable dropdown of all threads (including archived and closed) should be shown (same style as pinned messages). * Each thread should be represented by a box with the thread name, timestamp of last message and last message w/ sender PFP. * Threads should be ordered by last message (this does not update while the dropdown is open) * Right clicking any thread should provide a user with relevant context menu items (join, close, open, archive, unarchive, delete) ### Instance Level * Threads should appear in the admin panel just as channels do * In the “Message Tools” section, You should be able to input a ChannelID or ThreadID * “Browse Channel” should change to “Browse Thread” if the input is a thread. *Next to the “Browse Thread” or “Browse Channel” line should have the following: Channel Name (LINK) / Thread Name (LINK) / Thread started by: USERNAME (LINK) in Community (LINK) * Clicking Community name should hyperlink you to that Community in the admin panel * Clicking Channel name should hyperlink you to the “Browse Channel” page for that channel * Clicking the Thread name should hyperlink you to the “Browse Thread” page for that channel * Clicking the Username /ID should hyperlink you to the user’s page in admin panel * In the communities’ page, the channels section should include threads via a carat on the parent channel * The thread button should be half height to the channel button. * The thread button should be indented slightly to better showcase it as a thread * The thread button should contain the “THREADNAME - THREADID”, with the type on the right saying Thread * Categories should no longer be a shown as a full box. They should be just the “CATEGORYNAME (ID) in the upper left corner. * Channels, threads, and categories should be listed in the order as they appear in the instance.

Sub-issue of #1602 (Hub World epic).

## Why
Hub quests are mostly one-shot. A bounty board offers a renewable reason to play: rotating daily/weekly fetch & objective bounties that pay crystals/items.

## What to build
- A bounty-board interactable that offers N rotating bounties (seeded by date, like daily/weekly challenges) drawn from templates (collect X items, talk to Y, win a quick battle). Claim → track → turn in for crystals.
- Persist accepted/completed bounties and the rotation seed.

## Files
- `web/src/components/hub/` (bounty board modal + story), interactable in `config.json`
- `web/src/game/hub/` (new `bounties.ts`), reuse quest/pickup tracking; `docs/hubworld.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- Board shows date-seeded bounties; accepting tracks progress and turn-in pays out.
- Rotation refreshes daily/weekly; state persists.
- `npm run build` + tests pass.

Sub-tasks tracked as sub-issues.
title: Hub: repeatable bounty board

body:
a small suggestion for fun - the intent is to make longer and more interesting bounty routes.

The implementation I was working on used graph "colour coding". It's a stochastic fixed-length pathfinding algorithm, which I described as "effectively a depth first search with stochastic constraints".

I had some code at some point that changed bounty routes from node sequences to "route segments": node A -(colour coding)-> node B -(colour coding)-> node C...

initial naive algorithm implementation: https://gist.github.com/Trimatix/e468ba0cdc7d3002b6c41c3340ec0a3d
